phase3_findings.description: Nothing checks that the connector code actually calls require_setting; a later edit to tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py could return to os.environ.get(...) or None with an if-guard and silently drop the other-database checks without a skip, and the default run would stay green.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (one Suggestion and three inconclusive checklist items, none at or above the important threshold)

The PR is ready to merge: all 26 checklist items that could be decided passed, all 16 acceptance criteria were itemized, and no reviewer raised a finding at or above the threshold.
Rule applied: rule 6 — only findings below the threshold and INCONCLUSIVE items remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (1)

<details><summary>1 item</summary>

1. `tests/unit/test_connector_suite_contract.py` (lines 554-556 in the diff) checks `require_setting` on its own and scans the connector files for skip forms, but nothing checks that the connector code actually calls `require_setting`. A later edit to `tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py` could go back to `os.environ.get(...) or None` with an `if other:` guard; that silently drops the other-database checks without raising a skip, so every test in the default run would still pass. (raised by 1/5 agents)

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred

- VC-1: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — PyMySQL's 'rsa' extra exists and pulls in cryptography, which caching_sha2_password needs on non-TLS connections. [pyproject.toml]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  pyproject.toml:54-55 declares 'pymysql[rsa]>=1.1,<2' with the claimed comment. The claim concerns PyMySQL's own packaging metadata (rsa extra -> cryptography) and pymysql/_auth.py. No dependency_sources were supplied, the head view has no PyMySQL source or lockfile entry (Grep for name = "pymysql" found nothing; Glob for pymysql dirs under the review dir found nothing). Not verified: PyMySQL's pyproject optional-dependencies and _auth.py caching_sha2_password handling.

  </details>

- VC-3: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — Empty extras 'mysql = []' and 'all = []' are still advertised as provided extras, so pip installs '.[mysql]' / '.[all]' without the 'does not provide the extra' warning. [pyproject.toml]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  pyproject.toml:2-3 uses hatchling>=1.21 as build backend; lines 60-61 declare 'mysql = []' and 'all = []' under [project.optional-dependencies]. Whether hatchling emits Provides-Extra for empty extras lists depends on hatchling's metadata source, which is not in the views and no dependency_sources directory was supplied. I did not read hatchling/metadata/core.py nor build a wheel to inspect METADATA.

  </details>

- VC-13: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — Comment asserts ImportError messages are a module name only from a broken install missing a dependency [tests/unit/test_cli.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  src/sqllens/cli.py:144-145 returns str(exc) verbatim for any ImportError (allowlist at 76-82), so the test comment's universal 'ImportError messages are a module name only' (tests/unit/test_cli.py:1207-1208) is not enforced by code. CPython ImportErrors can carry more than a module name (e.g. 'cannot import name X from Y (/path)'), and a plugin could raise one with arbitrary text. But no unchanged requirement from another file shows this broken, and I found no shipped caller placing a config value in an ImportError, so no FAIL or INVALID can be established. The comment is an overstated description of a benign broken-install case; the test itself (pymysql message passthrough) is consistent with the code.

  </details>
